newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS - Pasminco unveils profit surprise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS - Pasminco unveils profit surprise.

text.p: The world's biggest zinc producer, Pasminco Ltd, on Wednesday reported a stronger than expected half-year profit on the back of higher sales premiums and a crackdown on costs.
Pasminco posted a net profit for the six months to December 31 of A$20.2 million, equalling the result it chalked up a year ago and exceeding an average market expectation of A$13 million.
"I think it's a bloody good result when you consider what the external environment has been," managing director David Stewart told a news conference.
Pasminco said it had weathered a virtually flat zinc price and a US$0.05 rise in the Australian dollar to an average of US$0.79, which combined to pare A$5 million from pre-tax earnings.
"The reason we've been able to maintain profitability is that we've further reduced costs and increased our premiums in the marketplace," Stewart said.
The cost drive took Pasminco's break even zinc price to US$895 per tonne, compared with US$900 per tonne for 1995/96 (July-June).
Stewart said Pasminco's smelting costs would continue to fall and it planned to look for rationalisation opportunities company-wide.

Zinc, which adds A$8.8 million to Pasminco's net profit for every US$25 rise in price, has rebounded in the current half while the Australian dollar has slipped about four U.S. cents from its 1996 peak of US$0.8165.

"If that were maintained, yes, that would give us a stronger six months but the market has been quite volatile so I am very cautious in predicting what they might end up at," Stewart said of current prices.
Pasminco's shares could not match the resilience of its earnings and at 0440 GMT (3.40 p.m.) they had slipped two cents to A$2.31.
But brokers said the entire resource sector of the Australian market was under pressure after an offshore slide in metals prices.

"It's not really gone down more than the others (other miners) frankly. I would call it more of a market-related thing, but it has come off its peak because of the Century situation," one Melbourne-based fund manager said.

Stewart said Pasminco had applied its cost focus to the Century Zinc deposit in north Queensland and it was hoped about 10 percent could be cut from the A$1 billion development cost originally estimated for the project.
"We hope to get it down at least 10 percent," he said.
He added the savings would be achieved by outsourcing some of the costs, including the mine fleet and power generation.
In January, Pasminco said it would buy the Century Zinc and Dugald River zinc projects from RTZ-CRA for A$345 million.
The Century sale is conditional on the Queensland government issuing mining leases which depend on Century Zinc Ltd and Aborgininal groups resolving a current impasse over land rights.
